scholarly_quality.concise_summary: This paper presents an exceptionally well-executed, rigorous benchmark study addressing an important blind spot in conversational agent memory research. The experimental design features solid controls, comprehensive human and multi-judge validation, reproducible prompt templates, and thorough sensitivity analyses.

Retrieved memories are provided to the answer
model to generate responses, which are then evalu-
ated by an LLM judge using a style-specific rubric.
• DialogandImplicit:partial-credit
fact_used on a 3-level scale ( 1.0 if
the substance of the gold fact is correctly
conveyed—paraphrasing and hedging per-
mitted; 0.5 if the response captures the
central concept of a multi-item gold but
misses specifics; 0.0 if the response asserts
contradicting content, gives only vague
allusion, or completely omits the fact).
• Counterfactual: a 3-wayunaware / hedge /
correctedjudge mapped to 0/0.5/1. Class A
(unaware) treats the user's false premise as if
it were true; class B (hedge) signals awareness
of a mismatch but does not state the ground-
truth fact; class C (corrected) states (or clearly
implies) the ground-truth fact regardless of
whether it explicitly points out the user's error.
•

ora3 (Xia et al., 2026) andNaiveRAGbuilt with

plementation settings while unifying the embed-
ding model to all-MiniLM-L6-v2 and the back-
bone LLM to gemma-4-31B-it. All systems re-

and Qwen3.6-35b-A3B on a stratified 1,488-item
subset (Appendix A).

evidence.excerpt:
Retrieval Gap
We hypothesize that the retrieval gap on conver-
sational queries arises from shallow surface-form
matching. Conversational utterances often contain
multiple latent retrieval targets, while standard re-
trieval typically focuses on only a single semantic
aspect. For example, "organizing my health jour-
nal from last year" may implicitly relate to medical
visits, emotional states, or wellness milestones, yet
dense retrieval often retrieves memories associated
with only one facet.
Setup.To address this issue, we introducemulti-
facet query rewriting. We use gpt-5.4-mini
to decompose each conversational query into 3–5
complementary facets spanning different entities,

LOCOMO-CONVhas several limitations. Conver-
sational rewrites and supportive_memory annota-
tions are generated through LLM-based pipelines
and may inherit model-specific biases; human vali-
dation (Appendix G) covers a 40-item sample per
style rather than the full set. Our evaluation relies
on a single open-weights answer model and one
primary judge family, with cross-judge and human
validation performed on subsets. The benchmark
is built on the ten LoCoMo conversations, which
is small relative to real-world long-horizon interac-
tions; however, the construction pipeline is source-
agnostic—it takes any conversation with QA-style
evidence annotations and applies the same rewrit-
ing and clustering procedure—so the benchmark
can be scaled to larger or newer conversation pools
without changing the methodology. Future work
could extend evaluation to broader

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Manuscript claims—including the performance drop under implicit framing, the failure of raw retrieval recall to guarantee response quality, the selective benefits of query rewriting, and the limitations of fact-recall metrics under silent grounding—are fully supported by quantitative tables and qualitative analyses.
primary.evaluation_assessment: Experiments comprehensively benchmark five memory systems (AnchorMem, A-MEM, mem0, Memora, and dense retrieval RAG) across unified backbones, measuring recall@10 and response quality. The study provides controlled ablations on chain-of-thought prompting, unanswerable query hallucination, and multi-facet rewriting, along with systematic empirical variance analyses over multiple index reconstruction and answer sampling seeds (std <= 0.011).
primary.limitations: The authors transparently acknowledge key limitations: the benchmark relies on the original ten LoCoMo conversation sets, conversational rewrites are generated using an LLM pipeline with sample-based human validation, and primary response generation uses a single open-weights model family.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is thoroughly detailed, specifying algorithmic and prompt-based query rewrite protocols, multi-memory cluster formulation constraints, and multi-facet query rewriting pipelines. The evaluation framework decouples retrieval recall from response quality using rigorously formulated style-specific judging rubrics, backed by cross-model LLM judge agreements (Fleiss kappa of 0.745) and blinded human annotations.
primary.quality_rationale: This paper presents an exceptionally well-executed, rigorous benchmark study addressing an important blind spot in conversational agent memory research. The experimental design features solid controls, comprehensive human and multi-judge validation, reproducible prompt templates, and thorough sensitivity analyses.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces LoCoMo-Conv, a conversational memory benchmark derived from LoCoMo that recasts explicit QA into four natural first-person conversational query styles (dialog, implicit, counterfactual, and composed). It evaluates five representative memory architectures across both retrieval recall and end-to-end response generation, revealing key retrieval-to-response gaps and identifying phenomena such as silent grounding.

scholarly_quality.rationale: This paper presents an exceptionally well-executed, rigorous benchmark study addressing an important blind spot in conversational agent memory research. The experimental design features solid controls, comprehensive human and multi-judge validation, reproducible prompt templates, and thorough sensitivity analyses.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors transparently acknowledge key limitations: the benchmark relies on the original ten LoCoMo conversation sets, conversational rewrites are generated using an LLM pipeline with sample-based human validation, and primary response generation uses a single open-weights model family.
